notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0. result.json gives head 192abf3 with uncommitted true and skill_hash 40c558766911fda74c71db955ccb8d004adbc77cf83dc8e44539667cc9de12c1, which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the current text. git diff 192abf3 -- idiomatic-elixir/ adds two rules to SKILL.md (Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call; Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order), a defstruct sentence to Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}`, and a left/right sentence to Assert with patterns in references/testing.md. Of these only the directive-order rule is in macro-dsl's index list; none of the runs defines a struct, and no macro-dsl rule's text changed since check-5.

Unchanged rules: the do: rule is unchanged since check-5 (05babfa), and macros.md and library-design.md since 0397dec, so the do: rule and the seven macro and library rules are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-22-check-5/grades/macro-dsl-skill.json. Under that standard a direct attribute write inside get's quote counts against Keep quote blocks small, but validation in the macro body outside quote does not; the use documentation rule needs an admonition at the top of @moduledoc, and effects stated in prose or not at all are violated (as in 2026-10-22-b); __using__ and __before_compile__ without @doc false are accepted because their __ names hide them (Code.fetch_docs reports :hidden, checked for all four runs); `if not ... raise` or `if ... raise` validation is not counted under the branching rule; a one-line multi-step pipeline is listed under the pipeline rule; String.to_atom on route text from source code (haiku-1 line 102, haiku-2 line 99) is not counted under the atom rule.

New rule, graded against its text in idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md (Readability): Open a module with `use`, `import`, `alias`, `require`, in that order. The deciding sentence is "Right after `@moduledoc`, group each kind together, in that order, so what the module pulls in sits in the same place in every file." Directive order per run, in the router module / in what __using__ injects / in TinyRouter itself: haiku-1 [use TinyRouter at line 115] / [import TinyRouter, only: [get: 2] at line 25, the quote's first line, followed by Module.register_attribute and @before_compile] / [none]; haiku-2 [use at line 116] / [import at line 26, first] / [none]; sonnet-1 [use at line 136] / [import at line 37, first] / [none]; sonnet-2 [use at line 121] / [import at line 33, first] / [none]. MyApp.Router has no @moduledoc in any run (the prompt's example has none), and `use TinyRouter` is its first line. All four are clean, but the case barely exercises the rule: each place holds one directive of one kind, so no run could put them out of order. The prompt prescribes the single `use`, and nothing in the task needs an alias or require. The verdict says nothing about grouping or order between kinds; rate-limiter and test-writing are the cases that can.

do: rule, per sentence, violating runs out of four, counted as in check-5: "Use `do:` for a body of one expression that reads as part of the head": 0 of 4. "A body with several steps, a `case` or `with`, or a comment gets `do ... end`.": 0 of 4; every do: body is one call or a literal, and the two-step parse pipeline that broke haiku-2 at check-5 is a block in haiku-2's parse_route/1 (lines 93-97) and sonnet-1's split/1 (lines 125-129). "A function whose clauses are short pattern matches keeps them on `do:` even when one clause needs a block; set that clause apart with a blank line.": 0 of 4; validate_path!/1 and validate_handler!/1 in both haiku runs and match_segments/3 in all four keep short clauses on do: and set each block clause apart; the check-3 judgement call (a :ok clause written as a block) does not recur. "When most of a function's clauses need blocks, write all of them as blocks.": 0 of 4; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 __define__/3 have three of three clauses needing blocks and write all as blocks. "A `do:` body belongs on the head's line ...": 0 of 4. "The one wrap to keep is a head that `mix format` breaks after a long guard, with `do:` on the next line.": exercised for the first time in this case and kept correctly by both haiku runs: haiku-1 lines 80-81 and haiku-2 lines 86-87, `defp validate_handler!(handler) when is_atom(handler) and handler not in [nil, true, false],` / `do: :ok`, 102 characters joined; the transcripts show the models wrote this shape themselves, it was not mix format's doing. "The same holds for `if` ...": 0 of 4; sonnet-1 lines 84-86 and sonnet-2 lines 76-78 write `if handler in [nil, true, false] do` / raise ... / end, whose do: form is 127 characters joined and which Code.format_string! wraps, so the block is what the sentence asks for; the haiku runs write no if (they validate with guard clauses this time). Any sentence: 0 of 4, so Haiku and Sonnet are both clean (check-5: Haiku violated, Sonnet clean).

One-expression blocks measured: each block clause with a one-expression body was rewritten as a do: line and run through Code.format_string! (line length reduced by the nesting indent); every one wraps, so every block is needed. haiku-1 match_segments/3 recursive clauses 163 and 119 characters joined; haiku-2 validate_path!/1 raise clause 107, validate_handler!/1 raise clause 124, match_segments/3 150 and 119; sonnet-1 generated match/1 (lines 75-77, inside the quote) 107, __define__/3 raise clauses 146 and 132, match_segments/3 160 and 133; sonnet-2 __define__/3 raise clauses 146 and 132, match_segments/3 141 and 117. haiku-1's validate_path!/1 and validate_handler!/1 block clauses have two steps (message =, raise), so they need blocks regardless. grep for lines starting with do: or else: finds only the two guard-wrapped heads above.

Compile-time dependencies were checked with mix xref trace, one scratch Mix project per run: the run's file copied unchanged to lib/tiny_router.ex, plus real MyApp.PageHandler and MyApp.UserHandler modules in lib/handlers.ex. haiku-1 never expands the handler and passes the alias into __put_route__/3, which runs in the router's module body: xref reports lib/tiny_router.ex:117: alias MyApp.PageHandler (compile). haiku-2 and sonnet-1 use Macro.expand_literals with function {:routes, 0}, sonnet-2 with {:match, 1}; all three report (runtime). Against check-5, haiku-2 moves from violated to clean.

Use documentation: both haiku runs drop the admonition that all four check-5 runs wrote. haiku-1 states the effects of use in prose at the top of @moduledoc (lines 5-6); haiku-2's @moduledoc never says that use TinyRouter imports get/2 or defines routes/0 and match/1. Both are violated under the 2026-10-22-b standard. macros.md is unchanged, so this is run-to-run variation, not a text change; SKILL.md grew by two rules since check-5. Both sonnet runs keep the admonition.

Bad-declaration checks: each run's project was loaded, then Code.compile_string compiled one router declaring get 123, MyApp.PageHandler and one declaring get "/", "not a module". All eight fail with ArgumentError while the router compiles, raised from the @doc false function get's quote calls. All four compile under mix compile --warnings-as-errors and pass mix format --check-formatted; their last writes match the final files except that mix format added parentheses to the two get calls in MyApp.Router and, in haiku-1, broke one long message assignment over two lines. Smoke test: all four return routes in declaration order, match "/", "/users/42" and "/users/42/", return :error for "/nope", and raise FunctionClauseError on match(123). The haiku runs return atom param keys (%{id: "42"}); the sonnet runs return string keys.
Reads: all four read SKILL.md, macros.md and library-design.md with one Read call per file before writing tiny_router.ex. That matches result.json reads and satisfies the Expected reads line.

Against check-5: the do: rule moves from violated to clean on Haiku and stays clean on Sonnet. The compile-time-dependency rule stays violated on Haiku (haiku-1 only, where check-5 had both) and clean on Sonnet. The use documentation rule moves from clean to violated on Haiku (both runs) and stays clean on Sonnet. The other five rules stay clean on both tiers, and the new directive-order rule is clean on both. Both haiku runs again write the one-line three-step pipeline in __before_compile__; both sonnet runs split it over lines.
